name: Ahaz
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Ahaz son of Jotham begins to reign over Judah and does not that which is right, but walks in the way of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel come up to war against Jerusalem and besiege Ahaz but cannot overcome him.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Rather than trust the Most High, Ahaz sends to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria saying, I am thy servant and thy son, come up and save me.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Ahaz strips the silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's treasures and sends it as a present to Assyria, who then takes Damascus and slays Rezin.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Ahaz goes to Damascus to meet the king of Assyria and sees an altar there, then sends its pattern and workmanship to Urijah the priest.
The true altar was made after the pattern of heavenly things given through Moses, but Ahaz copies a heathen altar he admired in Damascus.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Urijah builds the altar according to the pattern before Ahaz returns, and the king offers his burnt offering, meat offering, drink offering, and peace offering upon it.
Ahaz moves the brazen altar and commands Urijah to make the new altar the place of all the offerings, keeping the brazen altar for himself to inquire by.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Ahaz cuts off the borders of the bases, removes the laver, and takes down the brazen sea from off the oxen, dismantling the vessels of the temple.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: Ahaz sleeps with his fathers and Hezekiah his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

points: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years. Hoshea was the king of the northern kingdom. He began to reign in Samaria.

note.label: Abya Yala Under Fire

points: Hezekiah son of Ahaz begins to reign over Judah in the third year of Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the captivity.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Isaiah cries to the Most High and He brings the shadow ten degrees backward on the dial of Ahaz, reversing the natural course of the sun as proof of His power.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

points: He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign and reigned sixteen years, but he did not do that which was right in the sight of the Most High like his father David. He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and made molten images for Baalim.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: At that time Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him, for the Edomites had come and smitten Judah and carried away captives, and the Philistines had invaded the cities of the low country and the south of Judah and taken them. The Most High brought Judah low because of Ahaz, for he made Judah naked and transgressed sore against the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came to him and distressed him but strengthened him not. Ahaz took a portion out of the house of the Most High, the king's house, and the princes, and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him. Running to another nation for deliverance from the curses of God never works, then or now.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: Ahaz gathered up the vessels of the house of God, cut them in pieces, shut up the doors of the house of the Most High, and made altars in every corner of Jerusalem. This is the pattern of running to a nation that cannot save, the same spirit that trusts in the systems of the world instead of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: Ahaz slept with his fathers and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but not in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead. The Most High is the only one who can bring the people out of their condition, then and now.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

points: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are the days in which Isaiah prophesied.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: Ephraim joined Syria against Judah in the days of Ahaz. God said the plan would not stand.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: In the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up toward Jerusalem to war, but could not prevail against it.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: The Most High told Isaiah to go meet Ahaz, he and his son Shearjashub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller's field.

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: Ahaz said, "I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD." Isaiah answered, "Hear ye now, O house of David; Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?"

note.label: Isaiah 7: Ahaz, the Confederacy, and the Sign of Immanuel

points: The sign given was the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz brought back ten degrees. The prophet had told them it was a light thing to make the sundial go forward ten degrees, so instead the sun returned backward ten degrees as the sign to Hezekiah.

note.label: Isaiah 38: Hezekiah's Sickness and the Fifteen Added Years

points: The word of the Lord came unto Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

note.label: Hosea 1: A Wife of Whoredoms and the Sand of the Sea

points: The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

note.label: Micah 1: The Lord Cometh Forth Out of His Place

cases.name: Ahaz
cases.charge: Molten images for Baalim; burning his children in the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom; hiring Assyria with the treasure of the Lord’s house; sacrificing to the gods of Damascus that smote him; cutting the vessels in pieces and shutting up the doors of the house of the Lord
cases.preview: Ahaz son of Jotham walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, made molten images for Baalim and burned his children in the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom (2 Chronicles 28:1-4).
